purpose: Repair the two standing Brazil TSE and SNB source-scope defects before any further ordinary source-governance tranche.

set.institution: Presidency of the Republic of Brazil

set.rights_summary: Brazil Copyright Law 9.610/1998 art. 8 excludes official acts such as regulations and common-use information such as calendars/agendas from copyright protection.
set.automation_summary: Copyright status of official electoral-calendar facts does not itself establish unrestricted automated access to the TSE website; endpoint review remains required.
set.rights_review_note: Operational governance classification for WORLD SIGNALS; not a legal opinion.
set.governance_backfill_basis: TSE Resolution 23.760, as amended for the 2026 cycle, is the proper electoral-calendar provenance for first-round, conditional second-round and diplomation-deadline facts. Brazil Copyright Law art. 8 supports curated factual reuse of official acts/common-use calendar information; automated website retrieval remains a separate endpoint review.

set.endpoint_role: Forward event schedule — monetary policy assessments, news conferences and summaries
set.information_supplied: Exact forward publication dates/times for monetary policy assessment press releases, associated news conferences and summaries of monetary policy discussion
known_limitations: Dedicated event schedule is the forward timing authority; the decisions page is supporting context/history rather than the forward schedule.
SNB cadence and publication model is not Fed-like; assessment press release, news conference and later summary remain distinct linked series.
set.governance_backfill_basis: The SNB dedicated event schedule directly supports all 18 existing forward assessment/news-conference/summary occurrences through 13 January 2028. SNB non-commercial factual reuse terms support curated provenance, but automated access is not expressly granted and remains endpoint-review-required.

new_sources.institution: Presidency of the Republic / Portal da Legislação
new_sources.endpoint_role: Constitution art. 82 presidential term commencement rule
new_sources.information_supplied: Constitutional rule that the four-year presidential mandate begins on 5 January in the year following the election
new_sources.recommended_verification_cadence: manual annual/current-law recheck around election-cycle population and after constitutional amendment
known_limitations: Portal da Legislação content is informational and does not replace Diário Oficial da União publication; verify constitutional amendments through authoritative legal text.
Article 82 establishes the mandate commencement rule; it is not an electoral-administration schedule and must remain distinct from TSE calendar milestones.
new_sources.notes: Created solely to repair the provenance of WSO-EL-A-0004; no new canonical occurrence is authorised.
new_sources.rights_summary: Portaria 130/2021 permits Portal da Legislação content to be used, reproduced and shared with or without profit; derivative use requires source information and the portal is informational rather than a substitute for Diário Oficial da União.
new_sources.automation_summary: Content-reuse permission does not itself establish unrestricted automated retrieval behaviour; endpoint review remains required.
new_sources.rights_review_note: Operational governance classification for WORLD SIGNALS; not a legal opinion.
new_sources.governance_backfill_basis: Constitution art. 82, as amended by EC 111/2021, directly establishes 5 January as presidential mandate commencement in the year after election. Portal da Legislação reuse terms permit factual reuse, while automated retrieval remains separately unreviewed.

new_values.institution: Presidency of the Republic of Brazil

review_basis: TSE Resolution 23.760 is authoritative for the 2026 electoral calendar but does not establish the 5 January presidential term-start rule.
Brazil Constitution art. 82, as amended by Constitutional Amendment 111/2021, establishes that the presidential mandate begins on 5 January in the year following the election.
The canonical 5 January 2027 date and stable occurrence identity are unchanged; only provenance-semantic fields are corrected.
